caption:
West Africa's annual flood and pipeline-theft cycle is not random. It is structural, and public record explains most of it.

Dam releases from transboundary reservoirs upstream, most publicly documented around the Lagdo dam in Cameroon, are coordinated on a schedule that does not always match downstream warning timelines in Nigeria. That gap is administrative, not meteorological. Rainfall totals matter, but release timing decides when a surge actually arrives.

Pipeline theft follows its own logic: the arbitrage between crude price and refined product price on the black market persists regardless of enforcement surges. Interdictions raise the cost of theft. They rarely remove the incentive. Until that margin closes, the tapping will continue at a rate enforcement can suppress but not end.

Both patterns reward the same posture: watch the driver, not just the consequence.

card.headline: The calendar is not random
card.sub: Dam release timing and theft economics are structural, publicly documented drivers behind Nigeria's annual flood and pipeline crisis pattern.
